memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord has driven out before you great and powerful nations; to this day no one has been able to withstand you. One of you routs a thousand, because the Lord your God fights for you, just as he promised. So be very careful to love the Lord your God." — Josh 23:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua points again to the astonishing truth of Israel's victories: "One of you routs a thousand." No enemy could stand against them. But he is careful to name the reason — "because the Lord your God fights for you, just as he promised." The power was never in the soldiers; it was in the God who kept His word.

Then comes a striking turn. After all this talk of battles and victories, Joshua's central command is not "fight harder" or "be more disciplined." It is this: "So be very careful to love the Lord your God." Everything comes back to love. The safeguard against unfaithfulness is not fear or effort alone, but a heart that loves God deeply.

Notice the words "be very careful to love." Love for God is something we must guard and tend, not something we can take for granted. Hearts drift. Affections cool. So we are called to watch over our love for God the way we would protect a fire we do not want to go out.

This is exactly what Jesus named as the greatest commandment (Mark 12:30). And John reminds us that we love because God first loved us (1 John 4:19). The safest, strongest place a believer can stand is in warm, watchful love for the Lord. Guard that love carefully today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Would you say your love for God is warm, or has it cooled?
2. What helps you guard and rekindle your love for the Lord?
3. How does remembering God's love for you stir your love for Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for loving me first. Guard my heart from drifting, and help me to be very careful to love You with all that I am. Amen.
